thread:
Alex: heads-up — saw a latency floor on the eu-burst pool last night around 02:10 UTC. wondering where the best dashboards/traces are to check for KV cache evictions or subtle autoscale saturation. can someone point me to per-pool eviction heatmap, pending-queue trends, and the autoscale decision traces?

Maya: alex — for Grafana: go to Dedicated Pools > EU > burst-squad -> panels: 'KV cache: evictions & hit ratio', 'Autoscale: scale events & pending-queue', and 'GPU util by shard'. quick link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/pools?var-pool=eu-burst-squad (internal). also check the 'eviction heatmap' panel for time-bucketed spikes. :mag:

Sourav: tracing hint: use Jaeger, filter service=pool-scheduler and tag pool=eu-burst-squad, then look for spans named `scale_decision` and `enqueue_request`. PromQL I run locally:```
rate(kvcache_evictions_total{pool="eu-burst-squad"}[5m])
```and also:```
avg_over_time(pending_queue_depth{pool="eu-burst-squad"}[10m])
```if both move up that's a good saturation signal.

Jen: if evictions spike but GPU/CPU stay low, often it's many small requests thrashing the prefix cache. check `prefix_cache_hit_ratio` + `avg_kv_span_ms`. For alert tuning I'd propose changing the eviction alert to be compound: `eviction_rate > 0.5 /s for 10m AND pending_queue_depth > 50` to reduce noise. also add a suppressor for rolling deploys.

Liam: opened PR #2345 with the alert threshold changes + a link to a short runbook; pinging @Maya and @Sourav for review. short note in PR: 'we saw a 02:10 UTC blip where eviction_rate ~0.8/s but util stayed <40%'.

Maya: looking now, LGTM on the PR so far. also pin the 'kv-shard-steal-queue' panel on the pool dashboard — that was the early signal last time. :thumbsup:

Natalie: small ask — can we add a daily heatmap of request token-length distribution per pool? I think that would help identify when a surge of tiny requests causes a lot of small-cache misses. may be a separate dashboard or a derived metric.

Alex: thanks all. I'll attach logs from the 02:05-02:20 UTC window to the PR and start a short postmortem if we confirm autoscale misfire. assigning follow-ups: Liam (PR), Maya (review), Sourav (trace slice), Jen (alert wording).
